title: The Drawing House — the death-house two doors down the Clay Yard, Low Kiln, Sill
caption: The unnamed neighbour's house two doors down the yard from Vail, drawn close at the scale of a basket set at the edge of the light: the bench by the door with its pot, the draught going along the floor before the cold is felt, four nails, four and a thumb's-width knot overhead, the grey Ash ridge a finger's width thicker than Vail's and turning the corner by the door without a break. Inside, the drawing pallet against the far wall with the pale round place on the arm, the collector with the cold iron tube wrapped in wool and the slate face downward, a hearth, the folded quilt on the other side with the warmed stone at the belly and the pot set between child and door. The Vail kiln-house, wheel-shed, smithy, drying racks, House Silt, the birth-flower shrine, the yard well and the slip pits are drawn faint for neighbourhood; the Clay Yard and Clay Road run below, west to the Cross and east to Greybank. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Smoke, with compass, a hundred-pace scale, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the room that bears no name, the knuckle set before the iron and the note before the figure, and the child who grew worse before the day was out. An engraved cold-iron tube in its wool sleeve sits in the margin.
